project.name: GRASP
project.course: BCSE306L Artificial Intelligence — Case Study, Topic 16: Uncertainty-Aware Abstention in LLM Applications
project.one_sentence: GRASP detects which individual claims in an LLM's answer are likely hallucinated by reading the model's own attention patterns (plus the token probabilities it already produced), and does this better and more cheaply than the best published method (CCP) on the MUCH benchmark.
project.status_one_line: Supervised GRASP-v2 beats CCP on MUCH (0.924 vs 0.770) and, retrained in-domain, on RAGTruth (0.827 vs 0.623), at 33-38% overhead vs CCP's 192-430% on the same GPU. Zero-shot from MUCH to RAGTruth it only ties CCP; the training-free version does not beat CCP.

background_concepts.hallucination: When an LLM states something false or unsupported with the same fluent confidence as true facts. The model has no built-in 'I don't know'.
background_concepts.claim_level_detection: Instead of one score for the whole answer, give a risk score to each atomic claim (the smallest standalone factual statement). This tells you WHICH part to check or remove.
background_concepts.atomic_claim_example: 'Marie Curie was born in Warsaw in 1899' splits into 'born in Warsaw' (true) and 'born in 1899' (false; she was born in 1867).
background_concepts.ROC_AUC: Probability that a randomly chosen hallucinated claim gets a higher risk score than a randomly chosen correct claim. 0.5 = random guessing, 1.0 = perfect.
background_concepts.PR_AUC: Precision-recall area. More sensitive to how well you rank the rare positive class; depends on the base rate, so only compare it within the same dataset.
background_concepts.TPR_at_10pct_FPR: Share of hallucinations caught when you accept that 10% of correct claims are wrongly flagged. A practical 'how many do we catch' number.
background_concepts.confidence_interval: The 95% range the true value plausibly lies in, estimated by bootstrap (resampling generations 2,000 times). If the CI of a difference excludes 0, the difference is unlikely to be chance.
background_concepts.supervised_vs_training_free: Supervised = learns from labelled examples (here: claims labelled hallucinated or not). Training-free = uses no labels at all. Training-free methods are cheaper to deploy on a new model; supervised ones are usually more accurate.
background_concepts.attention: Inside a transformer, each attention head records which earlier tokens the model was reading when it produced the current token. It is a free record of 'where the model was looking'.
background_concepts.attention_sink: When a head finds nothing relevant to attend to, it dumps its attention on the very first token. High sink mass is a 'no-op' signal.
background_concepts.teacher_forcing: Re-feeding the model's own already-generated tokens through it in one pass, so we can read its attention without generating again or sampling.
background_concepts.abstention: Topic 16: a system should withhold or route for checking the claims it is unsure about. A good detector lets you withhold a small share of claims and remove most hallucinations.

the_benchmark_MUCH.paper: MUCH: A Multilingual Claim Hallucination Benchmark, arXiv 2511.17081 (Apache-2.0, École Polytechnique)
the_benchmark_MUCH.size: 4,873 generations, 20,751 claims, 4 languages (en, fr, es, de)
the_benchmark_MUCH.configs: 8 generation configs = 4 models x 2 temperatures (0.7 and 1.0)
the_benchmark_MUCH.split: train = 4,673 generations labelled automatically by GPT-4o and GPT-4.1; test = 200 generations also annotated by human experts (annotators an0, an1). MUCH stores no split field; we identify the test set by the presence of human annotator label keys, which gives exactly 200.
protocol_rules: the trailing end-of-sequence chunk is dropped
stopwords and punctuation are zeroed before aggregating token-level baseline scores
only claims where GPT-4o and GPT-4.1 agree are scored
the_benchmark_MUCH.what_it_ships: Claim boundaries (token_chunks), labels, the exact generated token ids, and the top-24 token probabilities for every generated token. This makes white-box methods possible without re-generating.

the_baseline_to_beat_CCP.name: CCP, Claim-Conditioned Probability (Fadeeva et al., ACL Findings 2024)
the_baseline_to_beat_CCP.idea: At each token, check whether the alternative tokens the model considered mean the same thing (paraphrase, so ignore) or something different (real factual doubt, so count it), using a natural-language-inference (NLI) model on every token.
the_baseline_to_beat_CCP.our_reproduction: ROC 0.7747, PR 0.6426 for ccp_24_8 / product aggregator (evidence: results/kaggle_run5/out/ccp_reproduction.json)
the_baseline_to_beat_CCP.cost: ~124% of generation time according to the MUCH paper (A100). Not yet measured on our GPU; that measurement is in progress.

three_attention_signals_per_token.G_grounding_ratio: Share of non-sink attention going back to the PROMPT rather than to the model's own freshly written text. Low = the model is riffing on its own output instead of retrieving.
three_attention_signals_per_token.S_sink_leakage: Attention mass dumped on the first token (the 'nothing relevant here' position).
three_attention_signals_per_token.P_dispersion: Normalised entropy of the attention row. Flat = no specific source.

the_method.head_selection_label_free: For each layer, keep the heads whose grounding ratio varies most across tokens on 200 unlabelled generations (a constant head carries no information). v1 kept 1 head per layer; v2 keeps the top 4.
the_method.GRASP_0_original: Training-free. Hand-weighted combination of G, S, P into a per-token risk, saliency weighting, soft-max over a claim's tokens, and a reset at claim boundaries. This was the original idea; it underperforms CCP.

features_per_claim: attention: 8 relative-depth layer bins x 4 heads x 3 signals x 4 statistics (mean, max, min, saliency-weighted mean) over the claim's content tokens = 384 numbers, z-scored per (layer, head) on unlabelled data
token probabilities (7 numbers): surprisal of the chosen token, entropy, top-1 probability, top-1/top-2 gap, taken from the probabilities MUCH already ships (no extra model run)
GRASP_v2_final.learner: Gradient-boosted decision trees (sklearn HistGradientBoosting, 31 leaves, 800 rounds), trained on MUCH's train split

the_method.GRASP_v2_free: Training-free variant: average of the per-model rank of mid-depth minimum grounding and the rank of token surprisal/entropy. Uses no labels.

what_happened_timeline.outcome: Report claimed GRASP-fuse 0.8343 vs CCP 0.8251, '1–3% / 6.4% overhead', and a German 'win'.

Found: no train/test split, fusion aggregator chosen on test data, a single-model German subset compared against CCP's 4-model pooled score, attention rows shifted by one token, saliency normalised twice, a sign error in the soft-min formula, and an estimated (not measured) overhead denominator. The original headline numbers were invalid.
Corrected attention alignment, single saliency normalisation, MUCH's real human-annotated test split, train-only tuning, cache metadata so settings cannot be mixed. Unit tests grew from 11 to 20.
GRASP-0 0.635 vs CCP 0.776 on only 136 test claims. CCP won; sample too small.

what_happened_timeline.step: v1: all 8 configs extracted on Kaggle (2x T4), supervised probe
what_happened_timeline.outcome: First read of the test split. GRASP-probe+CCP 0.891 vs CCP 0.770; attention-only probe 0.863. But the probe failed to transfer to unseen models.

what_happened_timeline.step: v2: 4 heads/layer + token probabilities + tuned trees, selection frozen on train
what_happened_timeline.outcome: Second read of the test split. GRASP-v2 0.924 vs CCP 0.770, no CCP needed, wins on all 4 models, transfers to 3 of 4 unseen models.

what_happened_timeline.step: Report, PDF, README rewritten; repo cleaned; git initialised

what_happened_timeline.outcome: RAGTruth fresh-benchmark confirmation with Mistral-7B-Instruct, and CCP timed on the same T4.

what_happened_timeline.step: RAGTruth confirmation (Kaggle run v9) + CCP timed on the same T4
what_happened_timeline.outcome: Retrained in-domain: 0.827 vs CCP 0.623. Zero-shot from MUCH: ties CCP. CCP overhead 192-430% vs GRASP 33-38%.

results_MUCH_test.test_set: 867 claims, 229 hallucinated, 200 generations (human-annotated split; scored against GPT-4o labels as MUCH's evaluator does)

transfer_to_unseen_model_roc.note: classifier trained on the other 3 models, scored on this model's test claims

runtime_overhead_T4.note: CCP and generation were timed on different sample generations, so overheads compare per token

what_contributed.evidence: results/dev/develop_v2_k4.json (train-split cross-validation, mean per-model ROC; CCP = 0.797)
takeaways: attention alone already beats CCP in cross-validation
token probabilities add information attention lacks
4 heads per layer beat 1 head per layer consistently (+0.01 to +0.02)
adding CCP as an input adds nothing, so CCP's expensive NLI step can be dropped

yes: Supervised GRASP-v2 beats CCP on MUCH's human-annotated test split: +0.154 ROC, CI +0.110 to +0.199, on all 4 models
Retrained on RAGTruth with the same frozen recipe, it beats CCP on a second benchmark: +0.203 ROC, CI +0.177 to +0.233, on all 3 task types
It costs 33-38% of generation time vs CCP's 192-430% on the same GPU
With in-domain labels it also beats pre-trained UHeads (closest prior method) on both benchmarks
At response level on MUCH: 0.911 vs CCP 0.762
no_or_not_yet: Zero-shot to a new benchmark it only reaches CCP's level (0.639 vs 0.623 after adaptation) and loses to pre-trained UHeads (0.680)
The training-free versions do not beat CCP at claim or response level
The original GRASP-0 idea loses to CCP

limitations_to_state: GRASP-v2 is supervised and needs labels from the setting it monitors
No zero-shot advantage across benchmarks/task families (RAGTruth)
The MUCH test split was read twice (v1 then v2); RAGTruth was read once, with rules fixed in advance
MUCH test labels are GPT-4o's, applied to the human-annotated samples, as in MUCH's evaluator
CCP vs generation timings come from different sample generations (per-token comparison)

novelty.closest_prior_work: UHeads / LUH (Shelmanov et al., EMNLP 2025): also supervised, claim-level, and uses attention + token probabilities, but trains a transformer head on attention maps.
what_is_new: first reported result beating CCP on MUCH
a much lighter learner: 3 interpretable attention statistics from label-free-selected heads + a small tree model on CPU
measured cost and cross-model transfer results
novelty.what_we_must_not_claim: that no prior method combines attention, token probabilities and claim-level scoring; or that GRASP beats UHeads (untested)

in_progress_now.status: nothing running; RAGTruth and same-GPU CCP timing are complete

next_steps: train on more diverse data to improve zero-shot transfer
retrain UHeads on MUCH for an identical-data comparison
re-run the novelty search the week of submission
